title: A Recently Fulfilled Order on the Profile and the Renew Bulk IT Refresh Wave It Reduces
content:
The machines a recent purchase holds back follow the profile's fulfilled orders, because machines that have only just been delivered are returned rather than traded. The orders in question are the profile's fulfilled orders under Northbeam Purchase Orders and Fulfilment, read for the day each was fulfilled and the balance standing outstanding on it. The recent purchase days are 30 days, counted in calendar days from the day the order was fulfilled to the day the matter is handled.

- Where an order on the profile was fulfilled within the recent purchase days and a balance stands outstanding on it, the machines held back are the unpaid order figure, being 4 machines.
- Where an order on the profile was fulfilled within the recent purchase days and no balance stands outstanding on it, the machines held back are the recent order figure, being 2 machines.
- Where no order on the profile was fulfilled within the recent purchase days, no machine is held back on that account.

**Both sides of the window.** An order fulfilled exactly 30 days before the day the matter is handled was fulfilled within the recent purchase days, so one of the first two branches governs. An order fulfilled 31 days before was not, and no machine is held back on this account.

**Both sides of the balance.** A balance stands outstanding where the order carries a balance above nothing; a balance of nothing is no balance outstanding, and the recent order figure of 2 machines governs instead of the unpaid order figure of 4.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A profile whose order under Northbeam Purchase Orders and Fulfilment was fulfilled 26 days ago and still carries 1730.00 USD outstanding holds 4 machines back from the Renew Bulk IT Refresh wave. The same order settled in full holds 2 machines back. An order fulfilled 74 days ago holds none back, whatever stands outstanding on it.
